teaching_blocks.title: The situation
teaching_blocks.content: Public security documentation should describe how the deployed API actually accepts authority, not advertise an undeployed way to acquire tokens.

teaching_blocks.title: The rule and its boundary
teaching_blocks.content: Declare HTTPBearer for a deployed bearer-token scheme so the generated OpenAPI securitySchemes entry describes token presentation rather than implying that the API issues passwords or tokens.

teaching_blocks.title: How to use the rule
teaching_blocks.content: For an established authorization-code issuer contract, configure OAuth2AuthorizationCodeBearer(authorizationUrl=..., tokenUrl=..., scopes=...) with the actual supplied issuer endpoints and permission descriptions. Describe the deployed authorization-code and PKCE acquisition contract where applicable, and do not present an OAuth2 password flow as production access guidance. Attach the scheme and required scopes through the real operation dependencies so generated operation security requirements agree with the authority the endpoint accepts. Inspect components.securitySchemes and each protected operation's security entry, checking issuer URLs, bearer presentation and required permissions against the deployed contract.

teaching_blocks.title: Reason through an example
teaching_blocks.content: For bearer presentation, declare HTTPBearer. For an established authorization-code issuer, configure OAuth2AuthorizationCodeBearer with actual supplied authorization and token endpoints and scope descriptions. Describe authorization code and PKCE where applicable, not a production password flow. Attach real operation dependencies and scopes, then inspect securitySchemes and protected operations' security entries against the deployed contract. Do not invent issuer URLs for the example.

teaching_blocks.title: Keep this distinction
teaching_blocks.content: A documentation scheme must agree with deployed authority. Bearer presentation does not imply the API issues passwords or tokens.

visual_anchor.purpose: Place the supplied deployed security contract beside the corresponding security declarations and generated components.securitySchemes and protected operation security entries, making bearer presentation, issuer URLs, and required permissions visibly comparable.

practice_anchor.objective: Document the supplied deployed bearer scheme and established authorization-code issuer contract using HTTPBearer and OAuth2AuthorizationCodeBearer. Preserve the existing verification and permission dependencies, connect the appropriate scheme and required scopes, and describe PKCE where applicable without offering a password grant.
practice_anchor.success: The generated security schemes describe bearer presentation and the supplied authorization-code endpoints and permissions accurately. Protected operation security entries match their existing dependencies and required scopes, and the acquisition description agrees with the supplied PKCE contract without advertising a password flow.

live_code.required_skill: Configure FastAPI security declarations and connect them through existing operation dependency graphs without changing the deployed authentication or authorization behavior.
allowed_syntax: def and async def dependency declarations
dictionary access to components.securitySchemes and protected operation security entries
blocked_syntax: TestClient(...) for authentication and authorization test cases
client.get(...) with invalid credentials to test token rejection
generated-schema traversal for unrelated contract drift or sensitive-field exposure
live_code.starter_state_intent: Provide the existing protected operation declarations, bearer verification and permission dependencies, and actual issuer authorization URL, token URL, scope descriptions, and applicable PKCE requirements. Leave only security declarations, dependency wiring, and acquisition documentation to complete; require no invented endpoints or new token-validation implementation.
live_code.observable_success: The completed declarations generate an HTTP bearer scheme and an authorization-code scheme with the supplied issuer URLs and scope descriptions. Each protected operation advertises exactly the authority required by its existing dependency graph. The accompanying acquisition description states the supplied authorization-code and applicable PKCE contract, with no password-grant guidance.
